CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 64-year-old female with psoriatic arthritis presenting for routine follow-up. She reports being on prednisone 1 mg daily, which appears to be an adequate dose. She occasionally takes an extra dose approximately once weekly when experiencing increased pain in her feet, particularly on days off work when she is more active. She has a desk job. She reports that methotrexate has been helpful for her joint pain. She previously held a dose of methotrexate during her first COVID vaccination due to concerns about vaccine efficacy but resumed it one week later, at which point she felt significantly better. She continued methotrexate for her second COVID vaccination dose after consulting with a hotline. She has noticed increased bruising on her skin, particularly in areas of minor trauma, which she does not feel when it occurs. She denies knowing the source of the bruises.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain in her joints and feet joints. Pain in knees had previously worsened but improved after increasing methotrexate dose. Denies other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily (to be discontinued).
Methotrexate (dose not specified).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works a desk job. She is more active and experiences increased joint pain on her days off.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Feet: Shoes and socks removed for examination. Patient reports mild pain in joints of feet. Good range of motion with toe flexion. Ridges noted in toenails consistent with psoriasis. Knees: Knee flexion demonstrates good range of motion without significant pain.

RESULTS
Not documented.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis, stable on current regimen. Plan to discontinue prednisone today given adequate pain control on current dose and concern for medication-related adverse effects such as easy bruising. Continue methotrexate. Patient to follow up with blood work prior to next visit (appointment to be made at front desk). Follow-up appointment in three months.
